title: Childhood trauma is the norm, not the exception, in prison psychiatric care
blurb: Records from 3,400+ adults in Dutch prison psychiatry found over half of men and nearly two-thirds of women had repeated trauma before 18.

title: How many teens develop PTSD after an earthquake?
blurb: A survey of 234 adolescents found most were resilient — but a meaningful minority showed real distress, with hyperarousal the most common symptom.

title: Cluster B personality disorders: what they are and what actually helps
blurb: A review of borderline, histrionic, and narcissistic PD — their origins, the therapies with real evidence, and why culture shapes both.

title: Kids with ADHD and autism face far higher mental-health risk
blurb: Across 14,000+ young people, those with neurodevelopmental disorders were 3 to 15 times more likely to also have anxiety, depression, or behavioral conditions.

title: Who drops out of DBT — and who improves?
blurb: Following 85 people through a DBT program, personality dimensions predicted both improvement and dropout better than symptoms alone.

title: The BPD brain is less flexible — and more variable
blurb: fMRI comparing 47 women with BPD to 28 controls found altered brain dynamics tied to childhood trauma and emotion dysregulation.

title: Can machine learning tell bipolar disorder from BPD?
blurb: Five studies, 591 participants: models beat traditional methods, but were far better at spotting bipolar than borderline.

title: Do demonstration videos actually teach therapy skills?
blurb: 123 psychology students were randomized to watch a video or reread the text — with a clear winner for learning technique.

title: What a violent hostage incident did to responders' mental health
blurb: Six months on, 192 police special forces and emergency personnel were assessed for quality of life and psychological impact.

title: A million genomes reveal what mental illnesses share
blurb: Rather than treating diagnoses as separate boxes, this study mapped the genetic architecture connecting them beneath the surface.

title: What drives stigma against tattooed people?
blurb: An Ecuadorian survey used factor analysis to unpack how tattoo stigma operates, especially within the justice system.

title: What separates forensic from general psychiatric patients with schizophrenia?
blurb: Machine learning compared the two groups to find what actually distinguishes them — beyond the offense itself.

title: Pinpointing where autism and schizophrenia genes switch on
blurb: A preprint mapping risk-gene activity to specific brain regions, not just broad cell types. Not yet peer-reviewed.

title: Is the thalamus different in schizoaffective disorder?
blurb: Detailed imaging broke the thalamus into sub-regions across schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, and healthy controls.

title: Two low-cost interventions for grandiose delusions
blurb: Indonesian nurse-researchers tested simple non-pharmacological approaches in a single case of schizophrenia with grandiose delusions.

title: A new 14-item scale for antisocial personality disorder
blurb: The SEPBA-APD aims to bridge categorical and dimensional approaches to diagnosing ASPD.

title: Virtual reality art therapy for borderline personality disorder
blurb: Eight participants completed four weekly VR-based art sessions, with wellbeing measured throughout. A small pilot, not proof.

title: Can a single dose of psilocybin help people quit cocaine?
blurb: A randomized controlled trial tested psilocybin plus structured psychotherapy for a disorder with no approved medications.

title: What GLP-1 drugs do to depression and anxiety
blurb: Swedish records for ~100,000 people compared periods when the same individuals were and weren't taking GLP-1 medications.

title: How early-life stress rewires the gut
blurb: A mouse model of maternal separation traced the actual mechanism linking early stress to long-term digestive problems.

title: Brain chemistry differences across anxiety disorders
blurb: 25 brain-imaging studies pooled to compare choline and other chemical levels across social, generalized, and panic anxiety.

title: Why some people hear voices: testing the inner-speech theory
blurb: A long-standing but hard-to-prove idea about how the brain fails to recognize its own inner speech, finally put to the test.

title: Schizophrenia genetics beyond European ancestry
blurb: Most schizophrenia genetics has studied European populations. This study set out to close a major gap in the science.

title: Finding the brain basis of BPD identity disturbance
blurb: Researchers studied identity disturbance as early as possible — before medication or comorbidity could muddy the picture.

title: Crying in therapy predicts better outcomes
blurb: Across 58 patients, those who cried more intensely and longer in early sessions reported better results later.

title: Cognitive training in mandated treatment
blurb: A 10-session group program combining cognitive and goal-management training, tested with 35 participants before and after.

title: Does the PTSD checklist catch symptom exaggeration across cultures?
blurb: 115 contractors were evaluated to test whether a common PTSD measure works outside Western populations.

title: Changing the wording changes your depression score
blurb: A randomized trial altered only the instructions on the PHQ-9 and GAD-7 — and the same people scored differently.

title: The self-esteem myth
blurb: A longitudinal meta-analysis of 27 studies found no robust evidence that low self-esteem causes later behavior problems.

title: Does vitamin D help depression?
blurb: 108 young people with both major depression and low vitamin D were given supplements. The effect was real but modest.

title: Treating moral injury in veterans
blurb: A pilot trial compared two therapies designed for the lasting pain of violating one's own deepest values.

title: An app for depression after breast cancer
blurb: 313 women were enrolled in a trial of a fully automated, publicly available program — because there aren't enough therapists.

title: Can a short video reduce suicide-loss stigma?
blurb: A large randomized trial tested whether brief video content could shift the judgment suicide-loss survivors face.

title: Group therapy measurably lowered cortisol
blurb: 60 adults randomized to an 8-week integrative group program — with the body's stress chemistry as the outcome.

title: 25 years of US adolescent mental-health deaths
blurb: CDC records for ages 15–24 from 1999 to 2023, tracking how mental illness figured into young Americans' deaths.

title: Does seeing clients more often help them finish PTSD treatment?
blurb: A meta-regression across 84 study arms asked whether session frequency drives treatment completion.

title: Mentalization therapy for antisocial personality disorder
blurb: A UK randomized trial offers cautious hope for a condition widely assumed to be untreatable.

title: Treating trauma and addiction at the same time in young people
blurb: Clinicians have long debated treating them one at a time. This trial treated both at once, in ages 12–25.

title: The real link between childhood maltreatment and narcissism
blurb: Across 2,157 people, early harm didn't simply 'create narcissists' — it shaped which narcissistic traits emerged.

title: Lifestyle medicine for depression, without a therapist
blurb: A three-arm trial of an 8-week program delivered by app, by booklet, or not at all.

title: The first non-dopamine schizophrenia drug in 70 years
blurb: Nearly every antipsychotic since the 1950s has blocked dopamine. A muscarinic drug works a completely different way.

title: Does EMDR really work?
blurb: A meta-analysis of 11 randomized trials: EMDR clearly beats no treatment, but roughly ties other active therapies.

title: There are two kinds of narcissism
blurb: Not every narcissist brags about being the best. Some brag about being the kindest.

title: Do psychedelics harm memory?
blurb: An exploratory study of working memory after a single dose. Reassuring — but it had no control group.

title: Younger substance users show more psychosis and violence
blurb: 264 patients followed for six months in Spain, comparing those whose use began early to longer-term older users.

title: Does trauma-focused therapy help when someone is also living with psychosis?
blurb: 305 people with psychosis and PTSD symptoms were randomly assigned to trauma-focused therapy plus usual care or usual care alone. Half of the therapy group saw their PTSD go into remission, compared to just 22% in usual care.
